chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Nu'man Al-Ahwal from Burayd Al-Ajli from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman on the condition that he teach her a chapter from the Book of Allah (Exalted is He). He said: 'I do not like that he consummates the marriage with her until he teaches her the chapter or gives her something.' We said: 'Is it permissible that he gives her dates or raisins?' He said: 'There is no harm in that, as long as she is pleased, whatever it may be.'

key_terms.سُورَةً: A chapter or surah from the Quran
key_terms.مُهُور: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on teaching the Quran as a dowry in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates teaching a Quranic chapter as a valid dowry (mahr), reflecting the Shia emphasis on knowledge as a tangible marital right. He advises completing the instruction or providing a material substitute before consummation to ensure clarity and satisfaction. The permissibility of modest gifts like dates underscores the flexibility in mahr valuation, provided the wife consents, aligning with the principle that mahr is a right of the wife rather than a fixed obligation.
